transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

No, it is not typically a fire risk. This warmth is normal for modern fridges as they dissipate heat from the cooling coils located in the sides. From what you have described, the most likely cause is dusty coils or too little space round it. Fridge freezers lose their heat through a coil or grille at the back or underneath. Gently dust or vacuum it, and leave a few centimetres of space between it and the wall or cupboards. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space round it?

I can't see any coils on the back, I haven't pulled it out as the floor is new and I don't want to scratch it. It's in a tight alcove, about 1cm each side and a few cm gap to the cupboard above. Is that enough space? There's no burning smell, if that helps.

No, a 1cm gap on each side is not sufficient for proper ventilation. Most manufacturers require at least 2-5cm of clearance around the sides and back to allow heat to escape. Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?
Both are cooling fine - the fridge is 4C and the freezer is -18C. I haven't seen any ice inside. It's only the outside sides and door frame that are warm.
Behind the rear panel inside the freezer, are the coils a solid block of ice, or fairly clear?
I'm not sure how to check that, sorry. I haven't taken anything off inside the freezer. Is that something I need to do? I'd rather not take it apart.

Yes, you should pull the fridge-freezer out from the alcove because the tight 1cm gaps are trapping heat and causing the sides to overheat. The appliance needs adequate airflow around it to cool down properly and operate efficiently. When you press the freezer door switch, do you hear the fan running, and are the coils clear or iced up?

I'd really rather not pull it out because of the new floor. I also don't know about a freezer door switch or fan, I haven't noticed anything like that, just the normal hum. Is there any other way to sort this without moving it?

No, you cannot resolve overheating caused by poor ventilation without creating space. The heat generated by the condenser coils must dissipate into the surrounding air, which is blocked in a tight alcove with only 1cm gaps. Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?

I haven't noticed any vents inside, so I can't say whether anything is blocking them. The food isn't packed especially tightly as far as I can tell. Still no burning smell or scorching. Is 1cm each side definitely too little, though? The manual says to leave space, but I haven't checked the exact figures.

Yes, a 1cm gap on each side is generally considered insufficient for adequate airflow. Most manufacturers recommend at least 5cm of clearance to prevent the sides from overheating and to ensure efficient cooling. Run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
I've run my fingers round both door seals and I haven't noticed any splits or gaps, so they seem fine. The doors close flat as far as I can tell.

Check nothing is stopping the door — a shelf, drawer, bottle or food sticking out — and that the door hasn't dropped or gone loose on its hinge. Most fridge freezers also need the front feet raised slightly so the doors swing shut on their own. Was something in the way or it not standing right (and have you sorted it), is the hinge broken or the door dropped, or does the door shut and line up fine?

Nothing is in the way of the doors, and they shut and line up fine as far as I can tell. I haven't checked the front feet though. Does any of this matter if it's cooling properly and nothing smells of burning?

Yes, the excessive heat on the sides indicates poor ventilation due to the tight alcove space. Even though it is currently cooling, restricted airflow will eventually cause the compressor to overwork and fail prematurely. Does it trip the moment you plug it in, when the compressor tries to start (a click/hum every few minutes), or after it has been running a while - and is there any burning smell or scorching?
